> Background General practitioners face high complexity in clinical decision-making. Large language models (LLMs) may support clinical reasoning, but their impact on decision-making processes and postgraduate medical training remains unclear. This qualitative study aims to explore General Practice (GP) trainee's use of LLMs in clinical reasoning and their educational needs. Materials and methods GP trainees were recruited and interviewed with semi-structured interview-guide. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and analysed qualitatively. Results Seventeen GP trainees participated (mean interview duration: 38 min; range: 21-63 min). AI was perceived as a tool to augment and accelerate clinical decision-making, while potential risks of deskilling were identified. This Perspective article argues that the OSCE final nursing score can be reinforced by adding a single global station examiner score to the checklist and by using a borderline regression method to derive a score based on a criterion. Drawing on selected literature on checklists and scales of global assessment, we outline the theoretical basis (Dreyfus model of learning and assessment), summarize comparative evidence and describe an illustrative hybrid scoring model using endotracheal tube aspiration. > Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong performance on multiple-choice questions but their ability to independently generate clinical decisions without pre-defined answer choices remains less established. We therefore evaluated LLM performance on post-graduate key feature questions (KFQs), which are designed to assess clinical decision-making at critical points. Thirteen LLMs were assessed in June 2026 using 30 novel hematology KFQs developed and reviewed by two hematologists with training in medical education. Each LLM was then asked to assess each case independently, with context reset between cases. Responses were subsequently evaluated for exact correctness and partial credit. Responses between models were assessed using mixed-effects regression, Cochran's Q test, and Friedman's test. Incorrect responses were classified as knowledge, decision, or comprehension errors and subsequently inter-model analysis was performed. Across 390 responses, exact accuracy ranged from 73.3% to 96.7%. This Commentary presents a preliminary, context-specific competency-based framework for anesthesia and intensive care education in Somalia, informed by a targeted non-systematic review of Somalia-specific sources and relevant international literature. > Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in critical care practice at a time when pharmacotherapeutic decisions are becoming more complex, data-intensive, and time-sensitive. For medical residents and fellows, this creates both educational opportunities and challenges, as AI may support learning but must not replace the development of independent clinical judgment. This perspective examines potential applications of AI in ICU pharmacotherapy training, including support for just-in-time learning, case-based practice, and bedside decision support. Key limitations and risks, such as misinformation, cognitive offloading, deskilling, privacy and data security, and bias in model outputs, are discussed along with possible mitigation strategies. Future training should prioritize building competencies related to AI-assisted clinical decision-making, including critical appraisal of AI-generated outputs and communication of AI-informed decisions within interprofessional teams. Tujuan penulisan adalah mengetahui integrasi AI ke dalam pembelajaran kedokteran, termasuk kebijakan, tantangan etika, dan implikasi pedagogi klinis. Metode penulisan berupa tinjauan pustaka naratif dengan menelaah jurnal terbitan 5 tahun terakhir di PubMed, ScienceDirect, dan Google Scholar. AI telah digunakan untuk simulasi pasien virtual, interpretasi radiologi, dan interpretasi pemeriksaan penunjang medis. Namun, percepatan adopsi ini tidak diimbangi dengan kebijakan institusional yang jelas. Tantangan etika berupa bias algoritma serta potensi penurunan kemampuan clinical reasoning mahasiswa karena ketergantungan pada AI. Di sisi pedagogis, peran dosen bergeser dari pemberi informasi menjadi fasilitator literasi AI. Oleh karena itu, diperlukan analisis mendalam terhadap kebijakan yang ada, supaya integrasi AI sejalan dengan pencapaian Standar Kompetensi Dokter Indonesia.

This article proposes a four-level analytical framework designed to transform diagnostic ambiguity into a prudent and auditable decision. In the first level (technical), "incurability" is delimited as a nosographic judgment based on treatment futility and traceability, as opposed to "irremediability" as a clinical-pragmatic judgment. The second level (phenomenological) defines irremediability as a 'frozen temporality' and a closure of the biographical horizon, where suffering becomes structural. > Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (CLL) is defined not only by disease biology but also by time. Its natural history reflects the pace of clonal evolution, the changing reserve of host immunity, the ordered use of therapeutic classes and the time patients seek to preserve outside illness and treatment. The expansion of highly active targeted therapies has shifted the clinical challenge from selecting an effective regimen to managing a longitudinal therapeutic trajectory. We propose a four-clock framework for CLL care. The clonal clock captures evolutionary tempo and biological urgency; the immune clock captures host immune reserve and recoverability; the therapeutic clock captures treatment exposure, resistance and preservation of future options; and the human clock captures patient-valued time, treatment burden and tolerance for uncertainty. Discordance among these clocks may be more informative than any single baseline risk factor. Therapeutic stewardship aims to align treatment intensity, duration, sequencing, monitoring and supportive care with the clock driving risk at each transition while minimising avoidable harm to the others. > In this paper the author argues that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has not created a new form of academic misconduct. Rather, it has taken the least-policed form of misconduct we had, that of cutting corners, and stripped it of the three properties that made it survivable. This 'sloppiness' was coupled to effort, bounded to one paper, and attributable to someone who lacked diligence. Fluent prose was once an 'honest signal', because it was costly to fake, and the apparatus of peer review built upon that cost. GenAI has broken that signal. > The term "experience" is widely used in health education literature. However, it has not been explicitly defined in this field, which could lead to multiple interpretations by researchers, teachers, and health students. Philosophical works offer clear definitions of "experience," which can provide useful theoretical insights for its appropriation in research, practice, and teaching. Notably, pragmatist, rationalist, and phenomenological philosophers John Dewey, Georges Canguilhem, and Maurice Merleau-Ponty define experience as the significance that emerges during the interaction between a subject and its environment. They distinguish between episodic (making an experience) and cumulative (acquiring experience) dimensions. The article further explores the implications of this definition in health education, particularly in relation to experiential learning, simulation-based education, and assessment. This conceptualization has also paved the way for a method of exploring experience designed to facilitate awareness, known as the "explicitation interview." > ABSTRACT Prison credentials can signal rehabilitation yet also disclose the records they aim to conceal. This study examines how a German open prison embedding vocational training in mainstream qualifications addresses this dilemma. Interviews with 14 inmates and two staff at Bochum‐Langendreer Open Correctional Facility underwent codebook thematic analysis. Inmates valued training for economic independence, especially chamber certificates concealing their origin. The facility managed the prison label through discreet concealment within the credential and brokered disclosure, vouching for inmates in the community. Their effectiveness depended on qualification level, migrant inmates' residence status, and economic conditions at release. Seeing prison as a “school of life” or “school of crime” reflected differing notions of school shaped by prior incarceration. The findings extend credential‐dilemma research beyond Anglo‐American contexts, offer the first German evidence on ethnicity and desistance orientations, and show credential design cannot substitute for the legal and social recognition desistance requires.

### The Future of AI Healthcare Governance: Towards a Risk- Based Liability Framework

- **Tags proposés** : Aucun tag proposé

**Mots-clés détectés :**

  - **ai_anchor** : artificial intelligence

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming healthcare delivery, but would you ever trust it more than your doctor? AI tools are being used for taking patient notes, doing predictive diagnosis and even robotic surgeries. They are shaping healthcare by making it more accessible and efficient. But they must be used with caution. Healthcare AI tools can show bias and raise concerns about data privacy and patient consent. The human touch is essential in health care,and AI tools are meant to assist, not replace, doctors. To effectively integrate artificial intelligence into healthcare, we need a risk-based framework which clearly outlines categories of risk while deploying AI and allocation of liability, given the extremely sensitive nature of the healthcare industry. However, existing legal frameworks governing medical liability don’t address this. This paper first examines the types of AI systems in healthcare and the legal problems associated with this deployment. It will also address the new way of looking at the standard of care, medical negligence and consent in healthcare. After examining the existing regulations, it will propose a risk-based framework for AI healthcare.

> Generative artificial intelligence has unsettled a quiet assumption on which assessment in higher education has long relied: that the work a student submits is a reasonable proxy for what that student can do. When a fluent essay or a plausible solution can be produced with little independent effort, the inference from product to competence weakens. Institutional responses have concentrated on integrity, detection, and compliance, and less on what sustained reliance on these tools may do to learning. Emerging evidence shows that performance with AI and learning without it can come apart, and we argue that the more important risk is therefore developmental: that some forms of reliance may bypass or, over time, erode the effortful thinking through which durable understanding and professional judgement are built. We treat this as a testable possibility rather than an established general effect. Building on programmatic assessment, we propose AI-Integrated Programmatic Assessment (AIPA). Based on expert consensus and newly available data, we have updated the previous 2024 clinical recommendations on the management of LRTIs in children and adolescents with SNI in Germany. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Background: Edema is a multifactorial clinical condition traditionally attributed to disturbances in vascular and lymphatic fluid dynamics. However, the contribution of respiratory mechanics to fluid regulation remains underrecognized. Objective: This narrative review explores the concept of respiratory-lymphatic coupling and its relevance to edema formation and persistence. Methods: Keyphysiological mechanisms linking breathing dynamics with lymphatic transport are examined, including the role of respiratory-induced pressure gradients and the thoracoabdominal pump in facilitating venous return and lymphatic flow. **Résumé / abstract :**

> To date, the field of computational psychiatry has largely focused on testing for dysfunction within lower-level cognitive processes in psychopathology, such as biases related to attention, reinforcement learning and memory. While this work has yielded important insights, there is clear evidence from empirically validated psychotherapeutic interventions to suggest that these lower-level cognitive processes are often intact. Here, we argue that etiological and maintaining factors for internalizing disorders may be more appropriately situated in higher level cognitive processes such as goal-selection. We further suggest that future research should incorporate behavioral tasks and models that allow for participant-defined goals to reveal higher-level mechanistic targets. We believe that considering these higher-level deficits in goal-selection, possibly in tandem with low-level impairments, may augment ecological validity and clinical relevance.

> Background and aims Neglected tropical diseases (NTDs) disproportionately affect the poorest communities, especially in Africa, yet global health strategies have consistently overlooked the significant mental health morbidity associated with these conditions. Despite the visible physical impairments, the associated mental and psychosocial burden, with depression and anxiety pooled prevalence estimated at around 38% in lymphoedema-related NTDs (leprosy, podoconiosis, lymphatic filariasis), and individual studies reporting anywhere from roughly 10% to over 70% depending on disease and setting, remains inadequately addressed in policy and practice. Beyond the impact of tobacco, LA faces unique challenges derived from environmental exposures and diverse genetic ancestry that shape a molecular landscape distinct from other regions. This has resulted in a high prevalence of actionable drivers, particularly EGFR mutations, positioning a large segment of the population as ideal candidates for precision medicine approaches. However, current efforts to address this epidemic fall short of regional needs, as the potential of precision oncology remains largely unrealized due to multilevel systemic and economic barriers. Entrapment typically occurs where these nerves cross rigid osteofibrous tunnels or pass beneath dense ligamentous structures, producing a deep, poorly localized pain that frequently radiates into the posterior thigh and mimics lumbar radiculopathy, a pattern often termed “pseudo-sciatica.” Because motor strength, reflexes, and dermatomal sensory findings are typically preserved, the condition is easily overlooked or misattributed to more familiar spinal or sacroiliac pathology, and patients often endure years of unexplained pain before an accurate diagnosis is reached. > Takotsubo syndrome (TS) as a manifestation of acute chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation is uncommonly reported. Emotional and adrenergic stress, hypoxemia, negative intrathoracic pressure, and the use of beta-agonists are frequently implicated in triggering myocardial dysfunction in this setting. We present a retrospective study of seven cases of TS in patients with COPD exacerbation in which none reported typical chest pain, representing a diagnostic challenge in patients with an apparent clinical justification for their dyspnea. All patients had electrocardiographic changes and elevated cardiac biomarkers, underwent echocardiography and coronary angiography or coronary computed tomography angiography, and received a confirmed diagnosis of TS. Five patients achieved complete recovery of ventricular function, one had partial recovery, and one died during hospitalization due to refractory ventricular arrhythmia. Systematic use of electrocardiography and cardiac biomarkers in COPD exacerbation enabled early diagnosis and appropriate management in the absence of typical angina.

> Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE), also known as Marantic endocarditis, is an uncommon complication of malignancy that may cause systemic embolization. We report a 74-year-old woman who developed a right gastrocnemius deep vein thrombosis followed by recurrent right middle cerebral artery occlusions requiring two mechanical thrombectomies. Her subsequent course was complicated by further deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and acute limb ischemia. Repeat echocardiography demonstrated mitral valve vegetations, initially raising concern for infective endocarditis. However, repeated blood cultures and cultures of retrieved thrombotic material were negative. Imaging revealed widespread metastatic disease, and biopsy of a left supraclavicular lymph node confirmed metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The combination of recurrent arterial and venous thrombosis, advanced malignancy, and negative microbiological investigations favored a clinical diagnosis of NBTE. This case illustrates how extensive thromboembolic disease may precede the diagnosis of pancreatic cancer and highlights the diagnostic challenge posed by valvular vegetations in this setting.

> Delayed diagnosis in primary care is usually discovered after the consultation has moved on: when a referral is accepted, redirected, rejected, delayed, or returned with an unexpected diagnosis. This Teaching Exchange describes the Referral Outcome Review, a tutorial method for GP specialty trainees that starts after the referral outcome has arrived rather than at the first consultation. The method was developed from routine one-to-one supervision and uses anonymised recent cases. Each case is discussed through six questions: (i) what was the initial diagnostic frame, (ii) what referral question was asked, (iii) what response came back, (iv) what uncertainty remained, (v) who owned the next step, and (vi) what patient-facing wording would be used next time? **Résumé / abstract :**

> Abstract Numerous reviews have mapped gamification and virtual reality (VR) research in medical education, yet none has systematically examined the semantic interrelations among themes or uncovered the structural imbalances in the knowledge base, as prior work treats topics as isolated and descriptive. To address this gap, this study applied bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERTopic) to 5,640 Web of Science articles, identifying 16 Topics across four categories: clinical skills, pedagogy, rehabilitation, and foundational competencies. Similarity analysis exposed a pronounced asymmetry: technology‑driven skill acquisition dominates, while cognitive foundations and meaning‑construction pedagogies are neglected. Based on these empirical patterns, this research propose a three‑tier Integrated Educational Functions Framework comprising Cognitive Foundation, Skill Acquisition, and Meaning Construction. This framework guides future research and practice, urging balanced investment across all tiers to foster critical thinking and equitable access in technology‑enhanced medical education.

The AI group used an ultrasound system with an AI module and received additional ethics and principles training, while the conventional group received standard training. Image acquisition and interpretation, debriefing time, trainee speaking time, and feedback were evaluated. Twenty-one trainee anesthesiologists were recruited (AI, n = 10; conventional, n = 11). It proposes an integrated framework linking Institutional Theory, Transformative Learning Theory, Stakeholder and Helix Models, and the Whole-Institution Approach. The framework explains SDG integration as a sequence of organizational adoption, pedagogical internalization, ecosystem resourcing and institutional embedding, all modified by a post-conflict lens. > Background The integration of genomics into clinical care has created an urgent need for accurate, standardized variant interpretation. Variant Scientists (VSs) play a central role in translating sequencing results into clinically actionable findings, yet formal education and standardized training pathways for this emerging profession are still evolving internationally. This study aimed to describe educational needs of practicing VSs and to develop a structured training program informed by those needs. Methods A national survey was distributed to practicing VSs across Israeli clinical genetics centers to assess training background, learning, access to interpretation tools, and professional challenges. > Lower-limb alignment is a key determinant of musculoskeletal loading and is associated with biomechanical risk pathways for conditions such as knee osteoarthritis and plantar fasciitis. However, routine alignment assessment still relies on radiography or specialist clinical examination, limiting scalability for early screening. Here, we investigated whether plantar foot morphology captured by weight-bearing 3D scanning can serve as a computational screening feature for proximal lower-limb alignment, and we developed a multimodal deep learning framework to support scalable alignment screening. We established a cross-sectional dataset of 167 participants (adults and children aged 6-60 years) with standardised plantar 3D foot scans and clinical labels for arch type, hindfoot alignment, and frontal-plane knee alignment. The proposed model jointly learns from plantar scan images and 16 geometric morphological features, integrated using feature-wise attention to prioritise alignment-relevant cues across modalities. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Abstract Musculoskeletal loss during spaceflight is well measured, while reconditioning after landing has rarely been studied. In 2016 the European Space Agency listed the unknowns of recovery from six-month missions, still unmet in 2023. This scoping review maps exercise-based reconditioning evidence from the recovery phase after spaceflight or a ground-based analogue against that agenda. Thirteen reports met the criteria, four of spaceflight and nine of bed rest. Their 32 results fall on four of eight in-scope parameters, and spine, cartilage and injury carry none. They completed 88 of 143 prescription fields, none stated a stopping criterion, and nine stopped measuring by the programme’s last day. Most recovery-phase data were collected by studies designed for other questions, and neither instruments nor thresholds have been standardised. Geriatric sarcopenia started from the same point and moved from a first consensus to outcome-tested cut-points within ten years, a path space medicine could follow.

Among the musculoskeletal manifestations, which are uncommon, vertebral sarcoidosis is extremely rare, while depicting a significant variability in radiological features. We present a unique case of a 52-year-old male, who was referred for MRI of the lumbar spine due to inflammatory back pain. Disc bulging at the intervertebral spaces L1/L2, L4/L5, and L5/S1 was found, without any signs of spinal stenosis or nerve root involvement. In addition, multiple small focal lesions were noticed in the vertebrae and the iliac bones, thus raising suspicion of bone metastases. Subsequent 18 F-FDG PET/CT showed neither evidence of primary tumor nor abnormal uptake in the vertebral lesions. No lytic or sclerotic pattern was recognized in CT scanning. Eventually, vertebral sarcoidosis was histologically confirmed by a nontargeted bone marrow biopsy of the iliac crest, performed as part of a standard hematological work-up, which is the diagnostic gold standard for this pathologic entity. Follow-up of the lesions with MRI scans showed stability over time, despite therapy with methotrexate.

> Regional anesthesia (RA) has become an increasingly important component of perioperative care in pediatric orthopaedic surgery. RA utilization in pediatric patients is well documented as part of the management of upper and lower extremity trauma, both at the time of fracture reduction as well as during definitive surgical stabilization. Elective management of both upper and lower extremity deformities and reconstruction of chronic injuries with RA support are common practices in many centers. Use of RA to mitigate postoperative pain and improve patient mobilization after elective spinal deformity procedures in pediatric patients is also well established. Despite extensive studies reporting successful and safe use of RA in his patient cohort, questions remain regarding potential risks and complications, particularly potential issues with postprocedure neurologic evaluation. Continued modifications in anesthetic techniques, in combination with an increased use of peripheral nerve blocks in place of neuroaxial blockades, may further limit the risk of potential postoperative issues.

> The orthopaedic total extraperitoneal (O-TEP) approach is an endoscopic technique that has recently emerged as an option, particularly for the surgical management of pelvic and acetabular fractures. Unlike conventional orthopaedic endoscopic procedures, O-TEP was developed by adapting the laparoscopic totally extraperitoneal approach, commonly used for inguinal hernia repair, to orthopaedic surgery. In technically demanding procedures such as periacetabular osteotomy (PAO), minimizing soft-tissue dissection and directly visualizing critical neurovascular structures are essential. **Mots-clés détectés :**

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Ulnar coronoid fractures often cause elbow instability, whereas conservative treatment risks stiffness. Traditional open surgical approaches are frequently associated with challenges such as inadequate exposure, risks of neurovascular injury, and heterotopic ossification. Although arthroscopic transosseous fixation offers a less invasive alternative, it may still cause fragment comminution, particularly when the bone fragments are small. This technical note describes an arthroscopic fixation technique using the capsular-fragment continuity. The procedure involves placing high-strength sutures through the anterior capsule. A bony tunnel terminating at the fracture bed (without traversing the free fragment) is then created in the ulnar shaft using a posterior cruciate ligament reconstruction guide. A suture passer is advanced from the tunnel's posterior exit, through the capsular-fragment continuity, to retrieve the high-strength sutures, which are secured over an Endobutton plate for fixation. This technique provides a safe, effective, and minimally invasive option for coronoid fractures, especially with elbow instability.

> The rapid advancement of wearable electronics places ever-increasing demands on the electrical and mechanical properties of materials. Cellulose offers renewability, low cost, and high durability for green wearables, but its weak electron-donating ability and poor charge-transport efficiency limit triboelectric performance. Inspired by the Janus structure found in sea urchin spines, a gradient-integrated triboelectric material (MWCNT/T-CNFs) was fabricated via vacuum-assisted layer-by-layer filtration. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Background Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) provides real-time anatomical and functional assessment during cardiac surgery and may detect abnormalities that require surgical intervention. Case An 80-year-old woman underwent minimally invasive left atrial myxoma excision combined with a maze procedure under general anesthesia. After weaning from cardiopulmonary bypass, routine TEE revealed a small but highly mobile echogenic structure near the right superior pulmonary vein. The operating surgeon was notified, and external palpation localized the finding to the superior left atriotomy, consistent with a redundant atrial tissue flap protruding through the suture line. Reinforcing sutures were placed to incorporate the flap into the closure and eliminate its protrusion into the left atrium. Repeat TEE confirmed complete disappearance of the lesion. The patient recovered without embolic complications. Conclusions Careful post-bypass TEE examination, including systematic assessment of atriotomy closure sites, may identify potentially embolic mobile echogenic structures and guide surgical management, thereby contributing to perioperative patient safety.

A 46-year-old female with chronic right lower back and buttock pain has CT scans which revealed right L4-L5 and L5-S1 facet joint arthrosis. After the patient received two radiofrequency ablation procedures, with the latter being less effective than the first, the patient's pain was still present. Because of persistent pain, cryoneurolysis was proposed as an alternative intervention. The patient experienced a similar degree of pain relief (pain level 8/10-3/10) as well as a more favorable acute postprocedural recovery. This depicts how cryoneurolysis represents a promising alternative neuroablative strategy for patients with lumbar facet arthropathy who have experienced inadequate relief following radiofrequency ablation.

> Magnetically actuated continuum robots (MACRs) have emerged as a promising approach for minimally invasive surgery. By using external magnetic fields to apply torques and forces at the instrument tip, MACRs move actuation outside the patient, thus reducing the mechanical complexity of the robot. This architecture enables miniaturization, improved compliance, and improved steering capabilities, especially for navigating intricate intravascular or endoluminal pathways. Despite substantial progress in functional materials, robotic archetypes, and magnetic field generation platforms, effective clinical translation requires holistic consideration of surgical workflows, intraoperative localization, and operator interaction. Integrating these engineering advances into routine clinical practice remains an ongoing challenge. > Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) management has evolved into a precision-medicine paradigm, with genetic risk factors such as TP53 and IGHV status serving as key determinants of frontline treatment selection. The therapeutic landscape has expanded to include fixed-duration options alongside established continuous regimens. This expansion has enabled personalized management strategies incorporating measurable residual disease-guided treatment approaches aimed at achieving deeper responses while minimizing long-term toxicity and resistance. In a relapsed/refractory setting, treatment selection must be guided by prior treatment exposure, identified molecular mechanisms of resistance, and the availability of novel agents. In this review, we have synthesized the latest clinical evidence and international guidelines to provide an updated, evidence-based algorithm for the diagnosis and management of CLL. Without a pre-formed expectation, scanning can become an open-ended search. This review proposes structuring image acquisition as a confirmatory task by linking a defined surface landmark to an expected sonographic target through a defined scanning path. The present article consolidates the correspondence between surface landmarks and sonographic targets, for a selected set of upper and lower limb nerve blocks used in orthopedic surgery, into a single landmark-based scanning algorithm. Four steps (anchor, place, trace, and confirm) structure each block: a surface anchor defines the starting reference; an initial transducer position is derived from it; a directional search vector defines the trajectory of probe displacement; and a sonographic endpoint confirms correct placement and marks the transition to the needling phase. Breast self-examination (BSE) is a feasible, zero-cost early-detection strategy for low-resource settings. Female medical students are expected ambassadors of this practice, yet adoption remains low. This study explored barriers and implementation strategies for regular BSE among female clinical medical students. A qualitative exploratory design using three focus group discussions (FGDs) was employed with 23 female clinical students at the University of Ibadan. > Idiopathic pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis (iPPFE) is a rare disease classified as a form of idiopathic interstitial pneumonia. iPPFE is characterized by upper-lobe-predominant fibrosis and a flattened chest wall, as well as distinctive clinical features including low body weight, absence of finger clubbing, a high incidence of pneumothorax, and a low prevalence of smoking history. Although vocal cord paralysis has diverse etiologies, iPPFE can also lead to recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy due to traction or compression of the nerve associated with apical-predominant pulmonary fibrosis. These findings may have contributed to recurrent laryngeal nerve dysfunction, although a direct causal relationship could not be established. > Hip arthroscopy has become the mainstream surgical treatment for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome, with approximately 88.75% of patients returning to sports postoperatively. Capsulotomy is a critical step in arthroscopic labral repair; however, various reported techniques possess inherent limitations. This technique employs an outside-in longitudinal capsulotomy along the femoral neck, followed by a transverse capsular release from its acetabular attachment along the path of the labral tear, creating an inverted "L"-shaped opening. On completion of the repair, the hip capsule is closed and retensioned using the remaining sutures from the labral repair anchors. This article summarizes the advantages, disadvantages, pearls, and pitfalls of this technique.

> Scapular reconstruction following tumor resection remains a surgical challenge because of the scapula's essential role in upper extremity biomechanics. Although patient-specific implants have expanded reconstructive options, achieving durable fixation and functional restoration remains difficult. A 14-year-old male with high-grade osteosarcoma of the scapular wing underwent limb-salvage surgery using a custom 3D-printed endoprosthesis. Preoperative planning incorporated dedicated software and patient-specific cutting guides. Wide resection preserved a small portion of the glenoid and the native glenohumeral joint to maximize postoperative function. At 3 months, radiographs demonstrated early osseointegration. The patient achieved 100° of active shoulder abduction without scapular winging or instability. At 2 years, he maintained near-full motion, demonstrated stable implant integration without loosening or recurrence, and returned to sports and daily activities with minimal limitations. Patient-specific scapular endoprosthetic reconstruction can achieve excellent oncologic and functional outcomes after subtotal scapulectomy, even in very young patients with high-grade malignancy.

> Background and importance Ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt placement remains a standard treatment of hydrocephalus, yet the commonly used method of freehand proximal catheter placement is associated with high rates of malposition. Although stereotactic navigation increases accuracy, it can introduce workflow inefficiency and increase intraoperative complexity. Augmented reality (AR) is an emerging technology that provides real-time integration of 3-dimensional imaging directly onto the surgical field. This report aimed to describe the feasibility and technical nuances of AR-guided proximal catheter placement using the Novarad VisAR system during a VP shunt surgery. Clinical presentation An eighty-one-year-old man with normal pressure hydrocephalus underwent elective VP shunt placement. Conclusion Proximal catheter placement was successfully accomplished on first pass using AR guidance. Postoperative computed tomography head confirmed accurate placement consistent with preoperative planning. This case illustrates the first use of AR guidance for presurgical planning and intraoperative placement of a proximal ventricular catheter and demonstrates the feasibility of this technique.

> Language processing is a highly complex dynamic neural activity that requires the recruitment of both regions critical for language processing and large-scale cognitive networks. Because language networks are interconnected and dynamically reconfigure their connections depending on task demand and complexity, it is challenging to differentiate language-specific networks form language-related cognitive networks during both resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) and task-based fMRI (tb-fMRI). Prior evidence demonstrated state-dependent differences in dynamic functional connectivity (FC) within identical networks across rest- and task-conditions. Based on this evidence, we hypothesized that examining dynamic FC patterns could help differentiate the functional specialization of large-scale neural networks in the human brain. > Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury is one of the most common knee disorders, occurring mostly in sports-related injuries. After injury, knee stability is compromised, leading to further damage to surrounding structures, such as meniscal tears, cartilage wear, and other lesions. Therefore, timely and effective repair of the injured ACL is critical. At present, a variety of surgical techniques are available for ACL reconstruction, with substantial differences in graft selection and fixation methods, and no universal consensus has been reached in the academic community. Hamstring tendons are among the most commonly used autografts. Preservation of the tibial insertion of the hamstring tendons has been proven to provide distinct biological and mechanical advantages. This technical note introduces an ACL reconstruction technique using a double-pulley system, which allows effective intraoperative adjustment of tension in each bundle of the reconstructed ACL to achieve highly uniform tension across all bundles. > Purpose To identify the common patient questions and to evaluate the quality of online resources regarding peptide therapy, namely, body protection compound-157, in orthopaedic surgery. Methods Three orthopaedic peptide searches were entered into a clean Google Web Search on June 30, 2025. Questions under the "People also ask" tab were expanded sequentially. The first 100 consecutive results meeting inclusion criteria for each query were included (300 total). Questions were categorized into 1 of 3 Rothwell Classifications and subcategorized by topic. Websites were categorized based on source. This narrative review examines the clinical evidence for ticagrelor-associated central sleep apnea and the respiratory-control mechanisms proposed to underlie this association. A structured literature search was performed using PubMed, with Google Scholar and citation tracking used for supplementary discovery. Overall, the literature supports a possible association between ticagrelor exposure and central respiratory instability, although the incidence, clinical significance, and susceptibility factors remain uncertain. **Mots-clés détectés :**

  - **low_priority_clinical_topics** : gynecologic
  - **negative_keywords** : surgery, cancer

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Sexual dysfunction, defined as a clinically significant and persistent disturbance in sexual desire, arousal, orgasm, or pain during sexual activity, affects up to 90% of gynecologic cancer survivors. Sexual health is a well-established component of quality of life, and its assessment should be routinely integrated into survivorship care. Treatment with surgery, chemotherapy, and/or radiation can result in early menopause, disruption of pelvic vasculature and nerve innovation, and alteration of pelvic anatomy that profoundly impacts sexual health. These physical consequences from treatment can compound the psychological burden that accompanies a cancer diagnosis. Here we review the evidence and provide recommendations for the evaluation and management of sexual dysfunction following the diagnosis and treatment of gynecologic cancer. We will discuss the mechanisms by which cancer-directed therapies affect sexual health, multimodal symptom-based treatment approaches, and lastly highlights awareness for continued areas of advocacy with the goal of providing all patients with comprehensive survivorship care.

> Root resorption (RR) involves the loss of mineralized root tissues and may compromise tooth integrity and long-term retention. Internal and external RR arise in different pulpal and periodontal microenvironments and require etiology-specific management. Although conventional treatment can arrest many lesions, persistent infection, complex resorptive defects, and limited control of inflammatory or clastic-cell activity remain therapeutic challenges. This narrative review summarizes RR classification, clinical management, and key mechanisms, including protective-tissue disruption, receptor activator of nuclear factor-κB ligand (RANKL)-dependent clastic-cell activation, inflammatory signaling, and mechanotransduction, and evaluates nanomaterial-based approaches by function. Potential benefits are weighed against cytotoxicity, local retention, effects on physiological remodeling, and the risk of inappropriate bone formation or ankylosis.
